\section[influir]{influir — to influence, to have an effect}

\label{lesson:ES-C583-influir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for consequently, then the Spanish for so.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: influir}
\textbf{influir} — \textquotedblleft{}to influence, to have an effect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El tiempo influye en mi humor.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The weather influences my mood.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{construir}: \emph{influyo, influye}. With \emph{en}: \emph{influir en algo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{influir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{influere} 'to flow in', built from \emph{in} and \emph{fluere} 'to flow' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{influir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{influir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{influir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for consequently, then the Spanish for so, then say \emph{influir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does influir mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To influence, to have an effect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la influencia]{la influencia — the influence}

\label{lesson:ES-C583-influencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for so, then the Spanish for to influence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la influencia}
\textbf{la influencia} — \textquotedblleft{}the influence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sus padres tienen mucha influencia en él.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{His parents have a lot of influence on him.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tener influencia en} or \emph{sobre} someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{influencia} is a learned word usually traced to Medieval Latin \emph{influentia}, first the power thought to flow in from the stars; it is built on Latin \emph{influere} 'to flow in' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la influencia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la influencia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la influencia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for so, then the Spanish for to influence, then say \emph{la influencia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la influencia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The influence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[afectar]{afectar — to affect}

\label{lesson:ES-C583-afectar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to influence, then the Spanish for the influence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: afectar}
\textbf{afectar} — \textquotedblleft{}to affect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La crisis afecta a todos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The crisis affects everyone.}
\end{quote}

With \emph{a} before people: \emph{afecta a los jóvenes}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{afectar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{affectare}, a form of \emph{afficere} 'to act upon', built from \emph{ad} and \emph{facere} 'to do' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afectar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afectar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{afectar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to influence, then the Spanish for the influence, then say \emph{afectar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does afectar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To affect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el factor]{el factor — the factor}

\label{lesson:ES-C583-factor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the influence, then the Spanish for to affect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el factor}
\textbf{el factor} — \textquotedblleft{}the factor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El precio es un factor importante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The price is an important factor.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Un factor clave} — a key factor.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{factor} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{factor} 'maker, doer', built on \emph{facere} 'to make, to do' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[generar]{generar — to generate, to create}

\label{lesson:ES-C583-generar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to affect, then the Spanish for the factor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: generar}
\textbf{generar} — \textquotedblleft{}to generate, to create\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La nueva fábrica genera empleo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The new factory creates jobs.}
\end{quote}

Common in news: \emph{generar dinero, generar problemas}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{generar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{generare} 'to beget, to produce', built on \emph{genus} 'birth, kind' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to affect, then the Spanish for the factor, then say \emph{generar} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Opiniones y razones}

\label{lesson:ES-R583-repaso-576-583}



\begin{quote}
Say the Spanish for to consider and to maintain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to consider, to maintain, the belief, the conviction, the stance
  \item to argue, the objection, convinced, reasonable, logical
  \item the disagreement, to disagree, to oppose, in favour, opposed
  \item to criticise, the criticism, to contradict, to admit, absurd
  \item the reason, as a result of, since, seeing as, given that
  \item to cause, to bring about, due to, because of, thanks to
  \item the consequence, the impact, to involve, consequently, so
  \item to influence, the influence, to affect, the factor, to generate
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To consider? (\textbf{considerar}.) To maintain? (\textbf{sostener}.) The belief? (\textbf{la creencia}.) The conviction? (\textbf{la convicción}.) The stance? (\textbf{la postura}.) To argue? (\textbf{argumentar}.) The objection? (\textbf{la objeción}.) Convinced? (\textbf{convencido}.) Reasonable? (\textbf{razonable}.) Logical? (\textbf{lógico}.) The disagreement? (\textbf{el desacuerdo}.) To disagree? (\textbf{discrepar}.) To oppose? (\textbf{oponerse}.) In favour? (\textbf{partidario}.) Opposed? (\textbf{contrario}.) To criticise? (\textbf{criticar}.) The criticism? (\textbf{la crítica}.) To contradict? (\textbf{contradecir}.) To admit? (\textbf{reconocer}.) Absurd? (\textbf{absurdo}.) The reason? (\textbf{el motivo}.) As a result of? (\textbf{a raíz de}.) Since? (\textbf{ya que}.) Seeing as? (\textbf{puesto que}.) Given that? (\textbf{dado que}.) To cause? (\textbf{causar}.) To bring about? (\textbf{provocar}.) Due to? (\textbf{debido a}.) Because of? (\textbf{a causa de}.) Thanks to? (\textbf{gracias a}.) The consequence? (\textbf{la consecuencia}.) The impact? (\textbf{el impacto}.) To involve? (\textbf{conllevar}.) Consequently? (\textbf{por consiguiente}.) So? (\textbf{de modo que}.) To influence? (\textbf{influir}.) The influence? (\textbf{la influencia}.) To affect? (\textbf{afectar}.) The factor? (\textbf{el factor}.) To generate? (\textbf{generar}.)
